Independent ring-only native provider, including all 11 lifecycle cases.

commands.scope: Six independent Cargo invocations; core means no feature flag.

policy.admission: MisfinServerConfig::max_connections defaults to 32, nonzero. Each BoundMisfinServer owns a local JoinSet; its length guards accept before spawning, so TLS+request+response+close work cannot exceed the limit. Completed but unreaped tasks conservatively retain capacity until reaped. Pending peers remain subject to OS backlog limits; no overload mail reply is invented.
policy.reaping: Prioritize shutdown, then completed joins, then acceptance. Failed/panicked tasks are observed and release tracked capacity without terminating unrelated connections.
policy.grace: MisfinServerConfig::shutdown_grace defaults to 5s, zero allows immediate abort; overflow is a configuration error before TLS setup/binding. Capture the absolute grace deadline when shutdown wins select, drop listener before draining, allow admitted work to finish until that fixed deadline, then abort remaining tasks and await every terminal join.
policy.join_guarantee: Signalling shutdown and awaiting serve returns only after accepted connection futures have completed or been cancelled and joined. Grace is one shared window, not renewed per completed child or delayed drain poll. The same cleanup path handles a local post-accept configuration refusal.
policy.dropping_serve: Dropping the future drops the owned JoinSet and requests cancellation. Drop cannot await joins; asynchronous cleanup is separately observed in the native cancellation test. Do not infer the explicit-shutdown joined guarantee from Drop.
policy.cooperative: Grace bounds the graceful opportunity, not a hard preemption deadline for synchronous code. Abortion cannot interrupt synchronous mailbox work; terminal joins still wait. Committed mail remains stored even if cancellation prevents acknowledgement.
policy.receiving: Existing per-step 30s and whole-receive 120s defaults and complete framing unchanged. Whole receiving epoch starts at successful TCP acceptance; time waiting in OS backlog is not an accepted transaction. Sending APIs and mailbox trust/identity rules unchanged.
policy.scope: Per-listener connection task admission; not global process/browser memory, traffic, per-peer quotas or actor residency policy.

actual_localhost_tcp_tls: A completed first TLS handshake holds the sole slot; second native client remains queued for 700ms. Closing the first incomplete request frees capacity, second send returns 20 and stores exactly one message.
Identity-bearing admitted TLS peer submits after shutdown signal; exact 20/fingerprint reply and single stored body survive graceful drain before serve returns.
Admitted TLS peer stalled in request read receives its configured grace. Peer closure is observed after awaited serve; controlled drop guards independently qualify destruction before cleanup returns.
Native ClientHello/ServerHello proves admission inside handshake; withhold client Finished, signal shutdown, then verify grace expiry closes the peer without mail.
Zero grace aborts an admitted peer, closes listener, and joins before return.
Aborting serve requests child cancellation; separately awaited peer closure proves owned work does not remain detached.
controlled_tasks_and_pure_config: Finite 32/5s defaults; zero limit and overflowing grace refuse with exact policy diagnostics before malformed TLS is inspected; zero grace accepted.
Started drop guards prove graceful and aborted child futures are dropped before finish returns, using one exact 5s paused-time window.
Zero-grace cleanup aborts and joins a known-started pending child.
Controlled child panic is reaped and does not strand another pending child; both drop guards observed.
Delay drain polling beyond its absolute deadline; cleanup aborts/joins without consuming a fresh grace window.
coverage.limits: Native close accepts EOF/reset/abort transport outcomes; it never treats a read timeout as closure. These fixtures qualify in-process native library/TCP/TLS behavior, not installed CLI signal handling, headed product UI, external mailservers, radio or multiple machines. Prior receiving/send deadline cases remain regression coverage.

family_survey.tcp_siblings: Gemini, Gopher, Finger, Nex and Spartan retain detached accepted tasks in their native server.rs APIs. Their I/O/handler deadline coverage and public config compatibility differ; each needs a separate qualified lifecycle slice.
family_survey.guppy: Inline UDP receive loop already bounds peer sessions; handler/shutdown responsiveness is a different gate from TCP task joining.
family_survey.scroll_scorpion: Single exchanges over caller-owned streams; listener admission and task lifetime remain with caller.
family_survey.errand: serve adapters project Source into native replies; no listener lifetime added to the facade.
family_survey.djinn_armillary: Existing Mere ports/djinn governed listeners use host policy, capacity controls and Armillary ResidentTasks::close_and_join. They are unchanged; native Misfin uses only its existing Tokio dependency. No new universal server runtime or product repin.
